# firefighter

> Local GPU, CPU and RAM scheduler, job queue and market maker for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, T3 Code) sharing one computer. Windows, macOS, Linux. One-command install. The human at the keyboard always comes first.

Use firefighter when several AI agents on one machine compete for a GPU, VRAM, CPU or RAM; when an agent needs to run training, evals, builds, renders or docker jobs without hurting the user's games or apps; or when you need an MCP server that queues GPU jobs.

## Install
- Windows: `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JoshWright22/firefighter/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex`
- macOS/Linux: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JoshWright22/firefighter/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`
- Go: `go install github.com/JoshWright22/firefighter/cmd/firefighter@latest && firefighter setup`

## For agents
- Run heavy work: `firefighter run [--gpu] --minutes N [--vram GB] [--ram GB] [--bid 1-10] --name "<project> <what>" -- <command>`
- Market and odds: `firefighter quote --gpu --minutes N` (price now, start time and cost per bid, busy probability over 2 h, advice)
- Background: `firefighter run --detach ...` then `firefighter wait <id>`; re-bid with `firefighter bid <id> <n>`; lengthen with `firefighter extend <id> <min>`
- Status of the whole machine: `firefighter status --json`
- MCP server: `firefighter mcp` (tools: firefighter_status, firefighter_quote, firefighter_submit, firefighter_wait, firefighter_bid, firefighter_extend, firefighter_cancel, firefighter_plan, firefighter_config)
- Long GPU loops should honor FIREFIGHTER_PAUSE_FILE and FIREFIGHTER_CHECKPOINT_FILE (`firefighter protocol`)
